segments: [page 399] to Malik al-Aziz his brother, who was ruling in Egypt;
and to Malik al-Zahir, his other brother, who was ruling in Aleppo;
and to Nasir al-Din, son of Taqi al-Din, his cousin, who was ruling in Hamat;
and to Malik al-Mujahid, son of Nasir al-Din, the son of his father's brother, who was ruling in Homs.
And he gathered forces from all of them,
and sent [them] with his uncle al-Adil.
And al-Adil came and encamped in the Meadow of Rayhan (Marj al-Rayhan), in the territory of Edessa.
And when Izz al-Din, the lord of Mosul, heard [of this],
he also gathered his partisans and came to Nisibis.
And there he fell ill with dysentery,
and he turned back and came to Mosul,
and after a short while he died.
For he was good by nature,
and merciful, and very modest.
No one ever saw him speaking
except with his eyes cast down before him.
Nor did anyone ask him for anything and he replied (and said):
"No."
And after him arose his son, Nur al-Din Arslan Shah;
and the one who was regent (and was) for him was Mujahid al-Din Qaimaz.
And in the year one thousand five hundred and five [of the Greeks],
which is 590 of the Arabs [1194 AD],
Ala al-Din Tekish, the Khwarizmshah, went forth to the land of Khorasan,
and Sultan Tughril met him near the city of Ray.
And Tughril was killed,
and his head was sent to Baghdad and hung on the top of a pole,
and it was fixed at the gate of the palace of the Caliph.
And the Khwarizmshah gained dominion over Hamadan and over the rest of the lands,
and he appointed as his deputy Qutlugh Inanj {OCR?}, son of Pahlawan,
the one who had previously ruled over Hamadan.
And he it was who had sent and brought the Khwarizmshah,
because Sultan Tughril had escaped from his imprisonment,
and had grown strong against him and taken the lands from him.
For with this Tughril the kingdom of the Seljuks in Khorasan came to an end,
and there remained this one near us in the land of the Romans [Anatolia].

For Tughril was the son of Arslan, son of Tughril, son of Mahmud (Muhammad), son of Malikshah, son of Alp Arslan, son of Dawud who is Chagri Beg, son of Mikhail, son of Seljuk, son of Duqaq (Tuqaq?). And in this year came Malik al-Aziz,
the lord of Egypt, against Damascus,
in order to take it.
